title: Pre-eclampsia, severe hypertension in pregnancy and eclampsia (India, FOGSI)
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Antenatal clinic, labour room, obstetric HDU, referral transport
summary: Screen every pregnancy with the HDP-Gestosis score and give aspirin 75 to 150 mg plus calcium to women at risk. Treat BP of 140/90 or more to a target of 140/90 or below, control severe hypertension with oral nifedipine or IV labetalol, give magnesium sulphate (Pritchard or Zuspan) for severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia, and deliver at 37 weeks (non-severe) or after 34 weeks (severe).

sections.title: Classify (FOGSI-Gestosis-ICOG)
items: Gestational hypertension: BP 140/90 mmHg or more after 20 weeks, normal by day 42 postpartum, without features of pre-eclampsia. Chronic hypertension: known, or detected before 20 weeks.

Pre-eclampsia: new hypertension of 140/90 or more after 20 weeks with significant proteinuria, or atypical pre-eclampsia with neurological, haematological, hepatic or renal involvement or fetal growth restriction without proteinuria. Superimposed pre-eclampsia: pre-eclampsia on chronic hypertension. Reconfirm BP after 4 to 6 hours before classifying, but never delay treatment of a severe-range reading (160 systolic and/or 110 diastolic): recheck within 15 minutes and treat within 1 hour.

Severe pre-eclampsia: BP above 160/110, or BP 140/90 or more with premonitory symptoms (headache, blurred vision, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, sudden weight gain, severe oedema) and/or abnormal HDP laboratory tests (low platelets, raised liver enzymes or creatinine, abnormal coagulation).
Early-onset pre-eclampsia begins before 34 weeks (more maternal complications, growth restriction and iatrogenic prematurity); late-onset after 34 weeks.
Significant proteinuria: more than 300 mg in 24 hours, dipstick 2+ or more, or urine protein to creatinine ratio 30 mg/mmol or more. Once established, repeated quantification is not needed.

Maternal alerts needing urgent action: persistent headache, blurred vision, breathlessness, vomiting with epigastric pain, uncontrolled BP, oliguria, brisk reflexes, altered consciousness, sudden massive oedema, SpO2 below 95%, LDH above 800 U/L, creatinine above 1.1 mg/dL, AST or ALT more than twice normal, platelets below 100,000/mm3, uric acid above 8 mg/dL.

sections.title: Work-up at BP 140/90 or more
items: Measure BP seated (or left lateral) with the cuff at heart level, after 2 to 3 minutes of rest; use Korotkoff V for diastolic (IV if V is absent) and a large cuff if arm circumference is above 33 cm.

Baseline HDP laboratory: urine protein (dipstick or protein to creatinine ratio), CBC with platelets, ALT, AST, LDH, bilirubin, creatinine and uric acid. Add coagulation profile if platelets are below 100,000/mm3, and electrolytes in severe disease.

Ultrasound: maternal (liver haematoma, ascites, effusions, renal disease) and fetal biometry, amniotic fluid, uterine and umbilical artery Doppler at diagnosis, repeated serially in confirmed pre-eclampsia or growth restriction.
Fundoscopy, echo, chest X-ray (with shield) or MRI brain only when indicated; neuroimaging is not needed routinely in eclampsia.

sections.title: Eclampsia: immediate steps
items: Call for help. Airway: left lateral position, mouth gag, suction, prevent injury. Breathing: oxygen, keep SpO2 above 96%.
Circulation: IV access, send HDP laboratory tests, Ringer lactate or normal saline at 80 mL/h, and a Foley catheter.
Give magnesium sulphate loading dose at once (below), then maintenance; control BP with antihypertensives; corticosteroids if below 34 weeks.
Deliver once the mother is stabilised after MgSO4; induce labour where feasible and reserve caesarean section for obstetric indications.

sections.title: Magnesium sulphate (all severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia)
items: Use 50% w/v ampoules (1 g per 2 mL ampoule). Continue for 24 hours after delivery or the last convulsion, whichever is later. Routine serum magnesium is not needed.

Pritchard (preferred) loading, 14 g total: 4 g IV as 20 mL of 20% solution (4 ampoules of 50% plus 12 mL distilled water) at 1 g per minute, plus 5 g of 50% deep IM into each buttock (with 0.5 mL of 2% lignocaine).

Pritchard maintenance: 5 g of 50% deep IM into alternate buttocks every 4 hours, only if patellar reflexes are present, respiratory rate is 16/min or more and urine output is 30 mL/h or more (more than 100 mL in the last 4 hours). On the Zuspan infusion, check the same hourly.
Zuspan (IV) regimen: 4 g IV loading as above, then 1 g/h infusion (5 g in 500 mL Ringer lactate at 100 mL/h, preferably by infusion pump).

Keep 10% calcium gluconate at the bedside whenever magnesium is given. Toxicity: stop magnesium, give oxygen, intubate if needed, and give 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate slow IV over 10 minutes with ECG monitoring.

sections.title: Antihypertensives
items: Treat BP of 140 systolic and/or 90 diastolic or more; target 140/90 or below and avoid hypotension. In severe hypertension lower BP promptly but gradually.

Severe: nifedipine 10 to 30 mg orally, swallowed whole (never sublingual, bitten or crushed), repeat in 30 to 45 minutes if needed, maximum total 120 mg, then switch to slow-release. Avoid in heart failure and AV or SA nodal disease.
Severe: labetalol 10 to 20 mg slow IV, then 20 to 80 mg every 20 to 30 minutes to a maximum total of 300 mg, or an infusion of 1 to 2 mg/min after the first dose; 200 mg orally if conscious.

Alternatives: hydralazine 5 mg IV or IM, then 5 to 10 mg every 20 to 40 minutes (infusion 0.5 to 10 mg/h); change drug if no response after 20 mg IV or 30 mg IM. Nicardipine infusion from 1.5 mg/h up to 6 mg/h.

Maintenance (non-severe): labetalol 200 to 1200 mg/day in 2 divided doses (first line, preferred if pulse above 100/min); slow-release nifedipine 20 to 120 mg/day in 2 to 3 divided doses (preferred if pulse below 100/min); methyldopa 500 to 2000 mg/day in 2 to 3 divided doses (stop after delivery because of postpartum depression).
Labetalol is contraindicated in asthma, heart failure and bradycardia (FOGSI also lists diabetes). ACE inhibitors, ARBs and diuretics are contraindicated in pregnancy.

sections.title: Timing and conduct of birth
items: Gestational hypertension: continue to term. Non-severe pre-eclampsia: deliver at 37 completed weeks. Severe pre-eclampsia: deliver after 34 completed weeks. Eclampsia and HELLP: deliver once stabilised.
Before 34 weeks, expectant management with steroids and close supervision may be individualised in a centre with obstetric HDU, blood bank, anaesthetist and neonatologist.
Corticosteroids if delivering before 34 completed weeks (and for elective caesarean before 38 weeks): dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly for 4 doses or betamethasone 12 mg IM 24-hourly for 2 doses.
Induce with prostaglandins or a Foley balloon; augment only with oxytocin. Caesarean for severe growth restriction, reversed end-diastolic flow, failed induction or obstetric indications.
Restrict IV fluids to 80 mL/h or 1 mL/kg/h (no fluid loading) to avoid pulmonary oedema. Always actively manage the third stage: these women tolerate blood loss poorly.

Before referral: Pritchard loading dose, nifedipine 20 mg slow-release or labetalol 200 mg orally, first dose of antenatal corticosteroid if indicated, and an escort with an eclampsia kit; inform the receiving centre.

sections.title: Postpartum and long-term follow-up
items: Monitor BP closely for the first 48 hours; eclampsia and HELLP can first appear after delivery. Avoid NSAIDs.
Treat persistent BP above 150/100. Treat BP of 160 systolic and/or 110 diastolic within 1 hour and consider magnesium sulphate.
After discharge: home BP monitoring and clinic review within 3 to 5 days, then close follow-up for 3 months with review of antihypertensives.

Advise contraception for at least 2 to 3 years (IUCD preferred) and preconception counselling. Advise long-term surveillance: pre-eclampsia raises lifelong risk of chronic hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, kidney disease and diabetes.

sections.title: Screen and prevent (HDP-Gestosis score)
items: Score risk factors early in the first trimester (full list in the GCPR). Examples: 1 point each for age over 35 or under 19, anaemia, BMI above 30, primigravida, PCOS, family history of cardiovascular disease, interpregnancy interval over 7 years, IVF or ICSI, MAP above 85 mmHg; 2 points for hypothyroidism, family history of pre-eclampsia, GDM, BMI above 35, multiple pregnancy, previous HDP; 3 points for pregestational diabetes, chronic hypertension, thrombophilia, CKD, autoimmune disease (SLE, APS, RA) or oocyte donation or surrogacy.
Total score of 3 or more: at risk for pre-eclampsia.
At-risk women: aspirin 75 to 150 mg daily, started early (ideally before 12 weeks) and continued until 2 days before delivery or caesarean section.
With aspirin, calcium 1 to 1.5 g daily for women with low dietary calcium intake.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Sublingual, bitten or crushed nifedipine, or rapid BP falls that compromise placental flow.
Missing atypical pre-eclampsia because proteinuria is absent.
Giving liberal IV fluids, causing pulmonary oedema.
Omitting the magnesium loading dose before referral, or giving maintenance doses without checking reflexes, respiration and urine output.
This protocol follows the 2019 FOGSI-Gestosis-ICOG GCPR; a 3rd edition (2026) has since been released, so check local adoption of any changes.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate (Pritchard)
drugs.dose: Loading 4 g IV (20% solution, 1 g/min) plus 5 g deep IM (50%) into each buttock; maintenance 5 g IM into alternate buttocks 4-hourly
drugs.notes: Maintenance only if knee jerks present, RR 16/min or more, urine 30 mL/h or more (above 100 mL in 4 hours). Continue 24 hours after delivery or last fit.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate (Zuspan)
drugs.dose: 4 g IV loading, then 1 g/h IV infusion
drugs.notes: 5 g in 500 mL RL at 100 mL/h by pump.

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.notes: Magnesium toxicity; keep at the bedside during magnesium therapy; ECG monitoring.

drugs.name: Nifedipine
drugs.dose: Severe: 10 to 30 mg orally, repeat in 30 to 45 minutes, maximum 120 mg. Maintenance: slow-release 20 to 120 mg/day in 2 to 3 doses
drugs.notes: Swallow whole; never sublingual, bitten or crushed.

drugs.name: Labetalol
drugs.dose: Severe: 10 to 20 mg IV, then 20 to 80 mg every 20 to 30 minutes, maximum 300 mg (or 1 to 2 mg/min infusion). Maintenance: 200 to 1200 mg/day orally in 2 doses
drugs.notes: Avoid in asthma, heart failure, bradycardia.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.dose: 5 mg IV or IM, then 5 to 10 mg every 20 to 40 minutes; infusion 0.5 to 10 mg/h
drugs.notes: Switch drug if no response after 20 mg IV or 30 mg IM.

drugs.name: Methyldopa
drugs.dose: 500 to 2000 mg/day orally in 2 to 3 divided doses

drugs.name: Aspirin (prophylaxis)
drugs.notes: HDP-Gestosis score 3 or more; start early, stop 2 days before delivery.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone or betamethasone
drugs.dose: Dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly for 4 doses, or betamethasone 12 mg IM 24-hourly for 2 doses

sources.title: FOGSI-Gestosis-ICOG Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy (HDP): Good Clinical Practice Recommendations 2019
